scheme_name: Assistance of Concentrate Feed After Parturition (General Category)
description:
The Assistance of Concentrate Feed After Parturition (General Category) scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2016. 

This scheme is specifically designed to provide financial assistance to dairy farmers. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the nutritional status of lactating animals. 

The scheme aims to enhance milk production by providing concentrated feed to dairy animals after they give birth. 

The government has set a measurable target of increasing milk production by 10 percent within the first year of implementation. 

The scheme is expected to benefit approximately 1 million dairy farmers across various states in India. 

Under this scheme, farmers are provided with a subsidy of INR 1,500 per animal. 

This subsidy is intended to cover the cost of concentrated feed for lactating animals for a period of three months after parturition. 

The assistance is aimed at both small and marginal farmers who own dairy animals. 

Eligibility for this scheme includes farmers who own at least one lactating cow or buffalo. 

Farmers must also be registered with the local dairy cooperative society. 

The age limit for beneficiaries is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There is no upper age limit specified for eligibility. 

Income criteria for this scheme stipulate that the annual income of the farmer should not exceed INR 2 lakh. 

Farmers must provide proof of income through income certificates issued by local authorities. 

The application process for this scheme is straightforward. 

Farmers need to approach their local dairy cooperative society to apply for the assistance. 

They must fill out an application form that is available at the cooperative society office. 

Required documents include proof of ownership of the lactating animal. 

Farmers must also submit an income certificate and a copy of their Aadhar card. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the officials at the cooperative society. 

The verification process typically takes about 15 days. 

After successful verification, the subsidy amount is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The disbursement is usually completed within one month of application approval. 

The scheme operates on a continuous basis throughout the year. 

Farmers can apply for assistance multiple times as long as they meet the eligibility criteria. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

This department is responsible for overseeing the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website. 

The scheme has been well-received by farmers, leading to an increase in the number of applications each year. 

In the year 2021, approximately 500,000 farmers benefited from this scheme. 

The total financial outlay for the scheme in the 2021-2022 fiscal year was INR 750 crore. 

This amount reflects the government's commitment to enhancing the dairy sector in India. 

The scheme also aims to promote better animal husbandry practices among farmers. 

Training programs are organized to educate farmers about the importance of nutrition for lactating animals. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt scientific feeding practices to maximize milk production. 

The scheme aligns with the National Dairy Plan, which aims to increase milk production in India. 

The National Dairy Plan was launched in 2012 with a target to increase milk production by 50 percent by 2025. 

The Assistance of Concentrate Feed After Parturition scheme contributes to this larger goal. 

It also supports the government's initiative to double farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme has been instrumental in improving the livelihoods of dairy farmers. 

By providing financial assistance, it reduces the burden of feed costs on farmers. 

This, in turn, allows them to invest in better quality feed and animal care. 

The scheme has been particularly beneficial in states with a high concentration of dairy farming. 

States like Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Punjab have reported significant increases in milk production. 

The government regularly reviews the scheme to assess its impact and effectiveness. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to make necessary adjustments to the scheme. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance food security in India. 

By improving milk production, it contributes to the nutritional needs of the population. 

The scheme also plays a role in promoting rural employment opportunities. 

As dairy farming becomes more profitable, it encourages more people to engage in this sector. 

Overall, the Assistance of Concentrate Feed After Parturition (General Category) scheme is a vital initiative. 

It addresses the immediate needs of dairy farmers while contributing to the long-term goals of the dairy sector in India. 

The scheme exemplifies the government's commitment to supporting the agricultural community. 

It provides a structured approach to enhancing the productivity and sustainability of dairy farming. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to improve their economic conditions. 

The assistance provided can lead to better health outcomes for both animals and farmers. 

In conclusion, this scheme represents a significant step towards strengthening the dairy industry in India. 

It not only aids farmers financially but also promotes better animal welfare practices. 

The ongoing support from the government ensures that dairy farming remains a viable livelihood option for many.
